newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end higher on high volume.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end higher on high volume.

text.p: Israeli shares closed higher on Thursday with traders saying that bullish investors were increasing their activity in the stock market.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.92 percent, or 2.60 points, to 284.92 on all-share turnover of 196 million shekels against 180 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.0 percent higher at 292.40.

"The bulls are kicking," said Idan Azoulay at Impact Union Portfolio Management. "The demand for stocks is rising and investors want to increase the equity weighting in their portfolios. It is clear that the market is strong and nobody wants to miss the momentum."
A trader at Tachlit securities said Thursday's session opened with a decline of 0.5 percent but that the market gained strength during the day.
The Tachlit trader said that new money was also coming into mutual funds specializing in stocks. "Most of it goes into funds that invest in small-cap stocks traded on the Karam index."
"Many companies are making secondary offerings, supply is rising and there is more free float, which shows that investors are showing more interest in the market," Azoulay said.
Azoulay added that a mild correction was needed but predicted the positive trend would hold steady. "We might witness a consolidation of one or two percent but the positive momentum will continue".
Africa Israel Investments surged 7.0 percent to 26,358 agorot. Traders said there was no evident reason for the rise. They noted that Africa rose on low turnover of only 804,710 shekels.

The most active shares were Bank Leumi, which lost 0.25 percent to 538 agorot on volume of 10.5 million shekels; Bank Hapoalim, which gained 2.0 percent to 799 agorot on turnover of 7.7 million shekels; and Clal Industries, which gained 0.25 percent to 1,756 agorot on volume of 7.1 million shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
